repo_notes.content: SCOPE — what this repository is and is not. Offhook is an iOS softphone application, not a library. It is the bring-up and debug client for swift-pjsua and intends to grow into a better-than-official PJSIP sample and a Swiss-knife softphone. The SIP engine is not here: it lives in swift-pjsua, which is itself layered on the prebuilt PJSIP binary from swift-pjsip. This repository contains only the app — the SwiftUI sources, Info.plist and privacy manifest under Sources/, the integration tests under Tests/, the direction documents under docs/, and project.yml. There is no .xcodeproj in git: the project is generated by XcodeGen from project.yml, which pins the two package dependencies to LOCAL sibling checkouts rather than to released versions. Do not generate pages documenting SIP, pjsua or PJSIP internals — those belong to swift-pjsua and swift-pjsip. Document the app: what it drives, how it is built and run, and the decisions behind it.
repo_notes.author: maintainer

repo_notes.content: AUTHORITATIVE SOURCES, in precedence order. The direction documents under docs/ are authoritative over code comments and over README.md's own summary, which says so explicitly. docs/Design.md records each architecture decision as decision, reason, and rejected alternative. docs/Roadmap.md is the Now/Next/Later milestone plan. docs/Tech-Debt.md is the numbered OH-# register of app debt, each item stating what it costs and which change discharges it; the IDs are OH-# specifically to avoid collision with swift-pjsua's TD-# register. docs/Provisioning-Models.md maps the mutually exclusive directions this app can take and names the one currently targeted. docs/Push-vs-Active-Socket.md is a decision record for a direction that is explicitly NOT built into the app today. docs/SIP-Test-Infrastructure.md says where to point the app to exercise the stack against real SIP infrastructure. docs/Credentials.md covers Keychain storage behind CredentialStore. docs/Prior-Art.md is a survey of OTHER softphones, recording per entry what was verified, what to take and what to avoid — its findings describe other people's code and must never be presented as this app's implementation.
repo_notes.author: maintainer

repo_notes.content: CONSTRAINTS and current status a reader must not miss. Offhook targets iOS 17 or later and needs Xcode 16+ and XcodeGen; run xcodegen generate before opening the project. The app deliberately owns the audio session rather than letting PJSIP open it — CallKit activates and deactivates the session and the engine's sound device follows — which is why the smoke procedure's success criterion is hearing the far end rather than merely reaching a connected state. Registration and dialling default to TCP because authenticated INVITEs fragment over UDP against the provider used for testing. Exercising the app needs real SIP infrastructure, a live registrar and an echo or loopback target, so the tests under Tests/ are integration tests against third-party providers rather than hermetic unit tests; a provider-side failure is an environmental condition, not necessarily an app defect. The current milestone is a Phase 0 smoke test — start the engine, register, place a call, hear audio — and much of the intended breadth is roadmap rather than shipped, so describe unbuilt milestones as planned.
repo_notes.author: maintainer
